narrative:
The model predicts you have a 79% chance of leaving your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outlook were your overall years of experience, whether you have received other job offers, and how long you have been with this current organization. These stood out clearly above everything else in shaping the decision.

Your six to ten years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees who stay have shorter experience (half have only one to five years), your mid-level tenure matches people who often explore new opportunities elsewhere. The fact that you have received other job offers also strongly pulled the prediction toward departure, as this is a common early warning sign of someone preparing to move on. Finally, having spent only one to five years in your current role added further weight toward leaving. Most employees predicted to stay have similarly short tenures here, but combined with your broader experience and external offers, it signals you may not be fully settled.

Your organization should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether additional responsibilities or changes could increase your sense of commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel like the right long-term choice.
